name: A — LLK monogram
prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: one polished logo concept for the open-source project DSLCompiler, presented on a clean pure-white square canvas for easy comparison.
Project meaning: custom LLK kernel semantics become a machine-independent tile execution IR called MicroIR; mappings to different hardware targets are explored by search, with feasibility and performance evaluation guiding selection.
Typography: exact project name "DSLCompiler", clean geometric sans-serif, dark ink, evenly kerned. A smaller descriptor below reading exactly "LLK / MicroIR". Do not add any other text. Place one generous emblem above the wordmark in a balanced stacked lockup with ample white space. The emblem should be about half the canvas width.
Art direction: original professional open-source compiler identity; strong distinctive silhouette; extremely crisp flat vector-like shapes; simple enough for a repository avatar at 48px. Solid deep navy and teal with a small amber accent marking the selected efficient path; no gradients, 3D, shadows, textures, glow, mockups, decorative circuit traces, stock chip pins, gears, robots, brains, magnifying glasses, or watermarks. No infographic, captions, explanation text, badges, or comparison sheet. One standalone logo only.
Concept A: KERNEL MONOGRAM. Create a bold compact square-ish emblem by custom-building the letters L L K from interlocking modular rectangular strokes. Two L-shaped blocks suggest kernel tiles; the K diagonals open into two target choices. One small amber tile at the upper diagonal endpoint marks the search-selected plan. The LLK lettering should be cleverly discoverable in a single coherent geometric symbol, not three ordinary font letters. Strong typographic craft, minimal parts, clean architectural negative space. The emphasis is the custom LLK dialect and modular compilation.
